location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::paragraph[1]

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::table-row[1]

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::table-row[2]

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::table-row[3]
sentence: | tmux is a terminal emulator in the middle: agent → tmux grid → re-emitted escape codes → browser xterm.js | double emulation causes fidelity bugs (repaint gaps, mouse/copy-mode weirdness) that we've been patching with refresh-client and sigwinch hacks |

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::table-row[4]
sentence: | one tmux server per user socket owns all sessions | a tmux server crash or wedge kills every agent on the host at once |

sentence: | control is subprocess-based (tmux send-keys, capture-pane, pane_in_mode polls) | per-keystroke subprocess costs we had to cache around (copy_mode_cached), and content transits argv/pipes of a third-party binary |

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::table-row[6]
sentence: | copy-mode intercepts input | browsers had to detect-and-cancel it (tmux::cancel_copy_mode) because a remote viewer must never be trapped in a server-side mode |

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::table-row[7]
sentence: | scrollback is line/grid-based | replay re-serializes the grid instead of replaying the byte stream the browser's emulator actually consumed |

location: ["sessiond-replacing tmux with purpose-built session workers","1. why replace tmux"]::paragraph[2]

location: []::heading-1[1]
sentence: spawn-trust architecture

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: this document defines spawn's trust model and the migration from a server-centric data plane to an operator model: the control plane negotiates identity, authorization, and connections, but is structurally unable to read the content that flows between a user and their machines.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: it is the governing document for the data-plane redesign.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: where design.md and this document disagree, this document describes the target and design.md describes the mechanics.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::heading-2[1]
sentence: the principle

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::blockquote[1]
sentence: the only parties that handle protected content are the host daemon, the user's browser(s), and-when nat requires it-a turn relay that carries ciphertext it cannot decrypt.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::blockquote[1]
sentence: the server introduces the parties; it never sees the conversation.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: "protected content" in this document means: pty input/output, scrollback/history, terminal snapshots and viewport controls; agent and host file names and contents; directory paths, entry sizes/mtimes, and operation errors; uploads, downloads, and cross-host transfers; tool check/install commands, executable paths, installed/latest versions, stdout/stderr, and detailed errors; agent and preset environment values; launch working directories/arguments; skill bodies; mcp credentials; and any label or error string derived from those values.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: everything on that list either already has an end-to-end path today or gets one in a migration phase below.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: the precise claim we are building toward is "the server cannot see your protected content" (cryptographic), not merely "the server does not look" (policy).

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: we do not use the unqualified phrase "cannot see your data," because the control plane deliberately retains the metadata disclosed below.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","the principle"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: each phase states which guarantee it delivers.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::heading-2[2]
sentence: roles

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","roles"]::table-row[1]
sentence: | party | holds | sees |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","roles"]::table-row[2]
sentence: | host endpoint (spawnd + workers) | session workers, ptys, encrypted bounded replay state, host identity key | everything on its own host (it is the user's machine) |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","roles"]::table-row[3]
sentence: | browser client(s) | rendered terminal, device identity key | protected content for hosts and agents it connects to |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","roles"]::table-row[4]
sentence: | turn relay | nothing durable | ciphertext, peer ips, traffic volume/timing |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","roles"]::table-row[5]
sentence: | control plane (spawn-server) | accounts, host/agent registry, public keys, signaling | disclosed metadata only, including coarse activity and unattended-update state; it also observes endpoint connection and traffic timing (see "what the server still sees") |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::heading-2[3]
sentence: why the cryptography already works in our favor

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: webrtc datachannels are encrypted with dtls negotiated between the two peers.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: the keys live at the endpoints; a turn server allocated for the session relays opaque ciphertext by design.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: so adding turn for reachability does not weaken the model at all-the fallback ladder

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: preserves end-to-end confidentiality at every rung.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: the parts that do not come for free:

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::list-item[1]
sentence: signaling integrity.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::list-item[1]
sentence: dtls authenticates the peers against certificate fingerprints exchanged in the sdp-which today flows through the server as rtc.offer / rtc.answer frames.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","why the cryptography already works in our favor"]::list-item[1]
sentence: a malicious control plane could substitute fingerprints and man-in-the-middle a session.

sentence: fixing this requires endpoint identity keys that sign the sdp (phase 3).

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::heading-2[4]
sentence: threat model

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: adversaries and what they get, once the migration is complete:

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[1]
sentence: | adversary | can | cannot |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[2]
sentence: | curious/compelled control-plane operator | see account + host/agent metadata, presence, connection/signaling timing and volume, user-input/meaningful-output times, and unattended-update metadata; refuse service; delete accounts | read pty data, transcripts, host or agent file data, viewport controls, tool details, env vars, skill bodies, mcp credentials |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[3]
sentence: | malicious control-plane operator (or compromised server) | everything above; record dtls/turn traffic; alter signaling or operator-hosted client code; attempt key-substitution mitm at pairing or signaling time | passively decrypt recorded dtls traffic when the negotiated suite provides forward secrecy and endpoint/session keys remain uncompromised; obtain the endpoint-local protected-store keys from server persistence.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[3]
sentence: phase 3 makes signaling substitution detectable only to trusted/verifiable endpoint code; it does not constrain hostile hosted javascript |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[4]
sentence: | network attacker (on-path) | observe/black-hole encrypted flows, learn peer ips | read or modify session content (dtls), impersonate either peer |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[5]
sentence: | turn operator | observe ciphertext volume/timing and peer ips | decrypt anything |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[6]
sentence: | malicious co-tenant | attack the api surface | reach another user's daemons or agents (all rest + ws paths filter by owner_user_id; daemon tokens are host-scoped) |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[7]
sentence: | attacker with the user's browser device | full access as that user |-out of scope; this is device security |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::table-row[8]
sentence: | compromised host daemon | everything on that host | other hosts' sessions (per-host tokens and keys) |

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: past-session confidentiality is not based on ciphertext being absent.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: a control plane, turn operator, or network observer can record ephemeral-session dtls ciphertext.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: its resistance to later decryption depends on the negotiated cipher suite's forward-secrecy properties and on endpoint/session key material not being compromised.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: phase 2 does not add a durable server-side ciphertext archive: restart manifests, preset operational values, and skill bodies are canonical on the host endpoint under docs/durable_sensitive_data.md, while the live worker replay remains separately bounded and ephemeral-keyed.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: a later optional opaque backup would need its own reviewed key/recovery threat model.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","threat model"]::paragraph[3]
sentence: explicitly in scope: protecting user content from spawn's own infrastructure and anyone who compromises or compels it.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: the device-code flow is already a pairing ceremony; it just doesn't exchange keys yet.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: target design:

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[1]
sentence: host identity: spawnd login generates an ed25519 keypair, stored beside the daemon token in the os keyring.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[1]
sentence: the public key is submitted with device/start and shown (as a short fingerprint) on the /device approval page, binding it to the user at approval time.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[2]
sentence: browser device identity: on first login, the browser generates a non-extractable webcrypto keypair (indexeddb).

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[2]
sentence: the public key is registered with the account.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[3]
sentence: signed signaling: every rtc.offer / rtc.answer carries a signature by the sender's identity key over an unambiguous, versioned canonical transcript: (protocol_version, session_id, scope_type, scope_id, sender_role, peer_identity_public_key, sdp).

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[3]
sentence: scope_type is agent or host, and scope_id is the corresponding agent or host uuid; the role distinguishes browser from daemon.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[3]
sentence: binding all of these fields prevents a valid offer or answer from being replayed across sessions, agents, hosts, protocol versions, roles, or intended peers.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[3]
sentence: each side verifies against keys pinned at pairing, so the dtls fingerprints inside the signed sdp inherit endpoint identity.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[3]
sentence: the forwarding server cannot alter this transcript undetected provided the endpoint verifier and its delivered build are themselves trusted/verifiable.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[4]
sentence: assurance levels (mirror how tailscale layers tailnet lock):

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[5]
sentence: l0 (today)-trust the server for introductions.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[5]
sentence: no content visibility once phases 1-2 land, but a malicious server could mitm at session setup.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[6]
sentence: l1 (phase 3)-signed signaling + tofu pinning.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[6]
sentence: for a trusted or independently verifiable endpoint build, server key substitution is detectable except at first contact.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[6]
sentence: operator-hosted, unverified javascript does not receive this assurance from protocol signatures alone.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::list-item[7]
sentence: l2 (later)-out-of-band verification ux (compare fingerprint shown by spawnd status with the web ui) and/or a key-transparency log, closing the first-contact gap.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","identity and pairing"]::paragraph[2]
sentence: key rotation and revocation ride the existing host revocation path (delete /api/hosts/{id}): revoking a host drops its token and its pinned key; browsers refuse sessions with unpinned keys at l1+.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: what moves where, and the regressions we accept:

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: scrollback/replay → endpoint-owned, resource-budgeted worker history rather than a new durable transcript archive.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: worker replay uses its encrypted-at-rest rolling log: the default 8 mib conservative total charge covers exact retained ciphertext/framing, twice the replay representation (return plus scratch allowance), and retained log/path bookkeeping.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: whole oldest segments are deleted before admitting new records; a checkpoint that cannot fit by itself is rejected.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: an admission/checkpoint failure disables and destroys replay for that live worker rather than retaining partial or over-budget history.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: the non-persisted key dies with the worker.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: the browser fetches the available tail over the datachannel at attach.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: a spawnd restart can adopt a surviving worker and recover only that retained history; once the worker and its history are gone, replay is unavailable.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[1]
sentence: server transcript.py and the content pubsub path are deleted; historical redis, files and backups remain subject to the purge runbook.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[2]
sentence: offline history → accepted regression.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[2]
sentence: the retired server path could replay a transcript while the host was asleep; after this cut, daemon offline = history unavailable.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[2]
sentence: mitigation later: optional client-side-encrypted transcript backup (browser holds keys, server stores ciphertext blobs it cannot read).

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[3]
sentence: live card previews → rendered client-side from per-host datachannel output.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[3]
sentence: offline hosts show status metadata only.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[4]
sentence: resize, scroll, redraw, and display ownership → per-agent spawn.ctl.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[4]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[5]
sentence: multi-viewer / multi-device → daemon fans out to n browser peers directly.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[5]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[6]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[7]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[7]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[7]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[8]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[8]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[8]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[9]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[10]
sentence: rest terminal surfaces → removed once direct replacements ship.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[10]
sentence: terminal input uses spawn.pty; history/snapshot uses per-agent spawn.ctl.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[10]
sentence: the server cannot implement a content-returning compatibility rest proxy without violating the model.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[11]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[11]
sentence: the store/key/recovery/conflict/migration decision is normative in docs/durable_sensitive_data.md.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[11]
sentence: the browser copies values directly between online hosts; the server is not a sync queue.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[11]
sentence: the migration must establish and restart-test a working endpoint copy before clearing the current plaintext database fields.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[11]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[12]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[12]

sentence: all three were removed (endpoint, registry + grants + their tables, oauth as + well-known metadata) rather than kept as an exception that falsifies the headline claim.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[12]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","feature relocation map"]::list-item[12]

location: ["spawn-trust architecture"]::heading-2[8]
sentence: residual risks

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::paragraph[1]
sentence: stated plainly, because a trust document that hides its weaknesses is worthless:

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[1]
sentence: web client delivery.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[1]
sentence: the hosted pwa is javascript served by the same operator the model distrusts; a hostile operator could ship exfiltrating js or disable signature/pinning checks before connecting.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[1]
sentence: consequently, phase 3's hostile-signaling-server guarantee applies only when the endpoint code is independently trusted or verifiable; an operator-hosted unverified web client remains an operator-trust endpoint.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[1]
sentence: mitigations, in increasing strength: open source + self-hosting (threat collapses to "trust your own machines"), reproducible web builds + signed releases, subresource integrity, and eventually a packaged client (pwa store build / tauri) whose update channel is independently signed.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[2]
sentence: first-contact key substitution until l2 verification lands.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[3]
sentence: metadata.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[3]
sentence: the control plane necessarily learns who owns which hosts, when they connect, coarse meaningful-output/user-input times, and the unattended-update metadata listed above.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[3]
sentence: the selected endpoint-local store avoids durable server-side object/version/access metadata, but its e2e transfers still reveal timing and approximate volume.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[3]
sentence: turn learns ip pairs and volumes.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[3]
sentence: we do not claim metadata privacy; self-host if that matters.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[4]
sentence: endpoint durable-store keys.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[4]
sentence: confidentiality and availability depend on the per-host key, recovery export, rotation, and destruction design in durable_sensitive_data.md.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[4]
sentence: key compromise can expose retained local versions; key loss without an export makes them unrecoverable.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[4]
sentence: a fallback key file stored beside the database does not protect a stolen full-disk image.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[4]
sentence: rotation does not erase old ciphertext unless old wrappers, backups, and keys are also destroyed.

location: ["spawn-trust architecture","residual risks"]::list-item[5]
sentence: endpoint compromise is out of scope and undiminished: an agent with your credentials running on your machine is exactly as dangerous as it is without spawn.
